title: A Inheritance for the Autopsy
premise: Paloma Lockridge, a concierge at the Hotel Verity who quietly solves guests' problems, is hired by a dying man named Aurel Sandoval to prove that a murder has not yet happened — his own, predicted in an anonymous letter dated thirty years ago. As Paloma investigates the letter's origins among the hotel's aging staff and a family of estranged heirs, he discovers the prediction was written by Aurel himself as a young man, confessing to a death he caused and swore never to repeat. When the predicted date arrives and Aurel is found dead anyway, Paloma must choose between protecting the woman he loves — Aurel's granddaughter, who may be the killer — and the truth, ultimately exposing that she acted to stop Aurel from repeating his old crime against her brother.
about_author: Lena Winterbourne spent a decade working night desks in grand European hotels before turning her eye for guests' secrets to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who watch for a living, and lives above a shuttered pensione with an unlicensed cat.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A gaunt stranger, Aurel Sandoval, checks into the Hotel Verity and pays triple to hire Paloma's unofficial services — not to solve a murder, but to prevent one: his own, foretold in a letter postmarked thirty years ago. Paloma, who never takes a case he can't close, accepts out of pride. Beat: intrigued unease.

chapters.title: A Letter Older Than Its Ink
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Forensic examination suggests the letter's paper is genuinely three decades old, yet the ink analysis is impossible — neither old nor new. The letter predicts death 'on the anniversary of the lilies.' Paloma begins mapping the hotel staff of thirty years ago. Beat: first crack in confidence.

chapters.title: The Granddaughter in Room 412
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Aurel's granddaughter, Mireille Sandoval, arrives unannounced, watching her grandfather with something between love and fear. She and Paloma share drinks; attraction sparks against his professional instinct to stay invisible. Beat: warmth shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Bellhops
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Interviews with retired staff reveal a fourth Sandoval sibling no one mentions — a brother who vanished in the summer of the lilies. The hotel's ledgers show Aurel visited annually on the same week, always alone. Beat: dread accumulating.

chapters.title: What the Concierge Saw
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Flashback chapter: young Paloma, newly hired, once glimpsed Aurel burning papers in the service courtyard and said nothing. His identity as 'the man who notices but never acts' is interrogated. Beat: guilt surfaces.

chapters.title: The Anniversary of the Lilies
chapters.summary: POV Mireille. Her perspective on her grandfather — tender memories braided with a childhood incident she can't fully remember: a garden, shouting, her brother's bandaged hands. Beat: unreliable tenderness.

chapters.title: Alibi, Woven Twice
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Aurel produces his own alibi for the predicted date — airtight, rehearsed, too perfect. Paloma realizes Aurel built it years ago. Why does a man pre-build an alibi for his own murder? Beat: inversion of the mystery.

chapters.title: The Heirs' Dinner
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The full Sandoval family convenes at the hotel: cousins, lawyers, resentments. Someone slips a second copy of the prediction letter under Aurel's door — meaning the sender is present, alive, and close. Beat: paranoia blooms.

chapters.title: Invisible Man, Visible Heart
chapters.summary: POV Mireille. Mireille admits she hired someone to follow Paloma first; she suspected him before trusting him. They become reluctant allies, then lovers, each hiding what they know about Aurel. Beat: love against duty established.

chapters.title: The Shuttered East Wing
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Paloma breaks into the sealed east wing, closed since the summer of the lilies, and finds a child's room preserved in amber — and scratch marks inside a wardrobe. Beat: horror beneath elegance.

chapters.title: The Confession That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Aurel (interleaved diary). Aurel's hidden journals reveal the truth in fragments: the vanished brother didn't vanish — he died, and young Aurel watched without intervening, then wrote the prediction as self-punishment: 'I will die as he did, unless I become better than I was.' Beat: tragic reframe.

chapters.title: Someone Rewrites the Ending
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The journal pages are tampered with — recent pages torn out. Only three people had access. The prediction letter wasn't a threat; it was a countdown someone else decided to enforce. Beat: stakes sharpen.

chapters.title: Mireille's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Paloma discovers Mireille lied about her whereabouts on two key anniversaries. Confronting her risks everything; not confronting her betrays the case. He chooses the case, and loses her trust. Beat: love against duty turns.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The family lawyer has been paying an annuity for thirty years to an unnamed recipient — hush money, or penance. Following the payments leads to a nursing home outside town. Beat: pursuit quickens.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't Dead
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The annuity's recipient: the siblings' former governess, presumed dead, who witnessed the brother's death and was paid to disappear. She confirms Aurel's crime — and adds one detail the journals omitted: there was a second child in the wardrobe. Beat: revelation cascade.

chapters.title: The Second Child
chapters.summary: POV Mireille. Mireille confronts her own buried memory: she was the second child, locked away by Aurel after witnessing the death, her trauma reshaped into tenderness. Her fear of her grandfather was never imagined. Beat: identity shattered and remade.

chapters.title: Countdown to the Lilies
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The predicted date is tomorrow. Security fails, allies scatter, and Paloma realizes the enforced prediction requires access only family has. He locks down the hotel — his hotel, finally claimed as territory rather than refuge. Beat: resolve hardens.

chapters.title: Night of the Anniversary
chapters.summary: POV alternating. The anniversary night: power cut, corridors dark, Paloma hunting through the east wing as figures move. He finds Aurel alive, waiting in the preserved child's room, dressed for his own funeral. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: What Aurel Wanted
chapters.summary: POV Aurel. Aurel confesses fully: he hired Paloma not to be saved but to be witnessed — a man who notices everything would finally see him truly. But the letter's enforcer isn't Aurel. Footsteps approach. Beat: climax ignition.

chapters.title: The Murder That Had Happened
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Aurel is killed before Paloma's eyes — by Mireille, who learned the full truth and believed Aurel intended to repeat his crime against her brother's memory, silencing the governess next. Paloma holds the evidence that could damn or save her. Beat: devastating climax.

chapters.title: Concierge, Closing the Case
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Paloma delivers the truth to the police with surgical precision — omitting nothing except the one mercy he can afford: framing Mireille's act as prevention, backed by the journals. Duty wins, but he bends it as far as it will go. Beat: costly integrity.

chapters.title: An Inheritance for the Autopsy
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Months later: the case closed, Mireille awaiting trial, Paloma inheriting Aurel's journals and the obligation to witness. He visits Mireille, gives her the one page she never read — Aurel's apology. Staying invisible was never an option; now he chooses to be seen. Beat: bittersweet resolution.
